To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eotaxin-3 expression is elevated in the mucosal lesions of patients with ulcerative colitis.
eotaxin 3 is a major eosinophil chemoattractant in the active lesions in patients with ulcerative colitis.

eotaxin-3 is a major source of colonic myofiroblasts in the colonic epithelia of IBD patients, and that the IL-4 and IL-13-induced eotaxin3 mRNA expression is regulated by STAT-6 and SOCS1-mediated pathways, and IFN-γ acts as a negatve regulator on the IL-4-and IL-13-induced expression via STAT-1 activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of eotaxins and the pathophysiology in inflammatory bowel disease.
the role of eotaxins in the pathogenesis of IBD.
the molecular mechanisms underlying eotaxin-3 expression in colonic myofiroblasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
eotaxin-3 may be involved in the pathophysiological process of UC.
the expression of eotaxins in the mucosa of IBD patients is regulated by the Th2 cytokines, and that this regulation is mediated by the activation of the STAT‐6 and SOCS1 pathways.
eotaxin 3 is a potential target for the development of therapeutic interventions in UC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eotaxin-3 expression was elevated in the active lesions in UC patients, and the expression was induced by Th2 cytokines in colonic myofiroblasts.
IL‐4, IL‐13, and IL‐4‐IL‐13 combination induce the expression of eotaxins in colonic myofiobroblasts, and IFN‐γ acts as negative regulators of eotaxine expression via STAT1 activation in these cells.
eotaxin-3 is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of UC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eotaxin-3 is upregulated in the active mucosa of patients who have ulcerative colitis, but not in those with Crohn's disease.
eotaxin-3 is a key player in the recruitment of inflammatory cells to the inflamed mucosal lesions of UC patients, and may play a role in the pathogenesis of UC.
eotaxin-3 is expressed in human colonic mucosa and that its expression is enhanced by T helper type (Th)2 cytokines.
